phase3_findings.description: New §1.4 dispatch-barrier local arm gates the inline fallback on 'the subagent has terminally ended with no return to collect' but supplies no mechanism to observe terminal-end vs still-running; a premature terminal-end judgement could fire the inline branch-setup fallback concurrently in the shared checkout.

Identical §1.6 issue-claim-auditor local arm: 'collect the completed return through the runner's own result-retrieval channel' states policy with no way to detect whether collection succeeded, is pending, or the channel is absent, so on a no-later-turn path no arm is explicitly defined.

Identical §4.0 deferral-drafter local arm: no mechanism distinguishes still-running from terminally-ended-with-no-return, so a mis-judged terminal-end could take the inline fallback while the drafter is still writing drafts into the shared checkout.

The failed-dispatch triggers plus 'still running' cover the state space only if the agent can observe those states; the prose supplies no detection mechanism, leaving the guard's fail-direction undetermined rather than provably fail-closed.

phase3_adjudication_note: code-reviewer: meets-standards, 0 findings. comment-analyzer: 0 findings; independently confirmed the retired-pins claim, the seven-barrier-site set, and byte-identity of the three new paragraphs. silent-failure-hunter findings are Medium/Low over agent-executed prompt prose: the change strictly improves the prior state (which had no guard and routed backgrounded dispatches to the concurrent-mutation inline path), the prose fails conservative-closed (inline fallback withheld while the subagent is still running), and it deliberately delegates state-detection to the runner's own channel because the issue forbids naming a runner-specific tool in shipped-verbatim consumer bodies. None rise to Critical/Important; verdict APPROVE.
